top.title: Passengers fear proposed biometric checks may cause chaos at domestic airports
top.description: By Dickson Omobola Federal Government’s proposed mandatory biometric checks for domestic air passengers from January 1, 2027, have come under scrutiny less than five days after the plan was announced, with passengers and industry observers warning that the policy could make air travel more difficult. They insisted that the plan appeared rushed and had not been properly thought through, particularly as the festive travel season would still be ongoing when the policy takes effect. They also feared that its implementation could trigger a repeat of the chaos that followed the introduction of the Go Cashless payment system, which caused hours of gridlock at airports in Lagos and Abuja. In March, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, introduced an electronic payment system known as Go Cashless at the toll gate of two of the country’s busiest airports. Its rollout left passengers travelling through the airports in Lagos and Abuja stranded for hours, triggering massive gridlock, missed flights and widespread frustration. While some travellers abandoned their vehicles at airport entrances after encountering difficulties completing payments, others said they missed scheduled flights after spending hours trying to gain access to the airports. The disruption prompted President Bola Tinubu to order the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Mr Festus Keyamo, to announce a suspension of the system on the fourth day of its implementation. With the busy Yuletide travel period extending into January, passengers and industry observers fear that a similar situation could unfold at the Lagos airport, the country’s busiest, especially as Keyamo has given domestic airlines until December 31, 2026, to integrate their operations with the system that will facilitate the biometric checks. Keyamo warned that airlines that fail to comply with the directive would not be allowed to board passengers from January 1, 2027. Known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, v-PASS, the biometric identity verification system is linked to the National Identification Number, NIN, of Nigerians. It is designed exclusively for domestic flights, with all passengers required to provide their NIN during check-in. Passengers are also expected to pay additional charges for the service. Speaking during the unveiling of the system at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos, Keyamo said: “I am giving the airlines till the end of December. I repeat it. top.title: No. 13 Oregon uses special teams trickery again to ignite another runaway win, thumps Michigan State
top.description: Oregon head coach Dan Lanning has overseen a midseason turnaround after the Ducks lost three of their first seven games. (AP Photo/Al Goldis) AP Photo/Al Goldis Long before No. 13 Oregon put the finishing touches on its 45-7 dismantling of Michigan State (3-8, 1-7 Big Ten) on Friday night in East Lansing, points were coming at a premium for the Ducks (8-3, 6-2). For the second time in three games, head coach Dan Lanning used special teams trickery to ignite a runaway win. With his team up 10-0 and seven seconds remaining in the second quarter, Lanning opted for a fake field goal on the final play of the first half. Instead of attempting a 33-yard attempt, kicker Gage Hurych received a pitch from his holder and, eventually, a block from tight end Jamari Johnson en route to the end zone. Hurych broke one tackle and crossed the goal line prior to going down. Lanning was elated, as were his coaches and players. The Ducks went on to score touchdowns on four of their first five drives of the second half. Their sixth and final series of the half consisted of a couple kneel downs. If we see it out there, we want to take advantage of it.” Oregon did the same thing at Ohio State on Nov. 7. At the time, the Ducks were trailing 14-3 to a No. 12 Buckeyes squad desperate for a bounce-back victory. Lanning was a facing a fourth-and-9 from his own 31-yard line. The 6-foot-5, 265-pound Uiagalelei barreled down the sideline and capped a momentous 30-yard gain with a hurdle. That drive ended in a touchdown and was a critical part of Oregon scoring 38 straight points in what wound up being a 41-28 win in Columbus . top.description: Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers survived a serious scare against the Sacramento Kings , escaping with a narrow 106-104 victory despite struggling to control the glass and protect their lead. Luka Doncic led the way with 25 points and eight assists, while Walker Kessler and Matisse Thybulle were solid on both ends of the floor. However, this was far from a convincing performance from Los Angeles, which allowed Sacramento to collect 44 rebounds and stay within striking distance. The Lakers shot an efficient 50.0% from the field, compared to Sacramento’s 45.6%, but their 30.6% shooting from three-point range left plenty to be desired. Los Angeles also had to overcome a 16-9 disadvantage in offensive rebounds, giving the Kings second chances throughout the night. The difference came at the free-throw line, where the Lakers converted 17 of 22 attempts compared to Sacramento’s nine of 12. Doncic had the biggest scoring night, but this victory was more of a collective survival effort than a dominant showing from the superstar. Six turnovers also gave Sacramento opportunities to capitalize, particularly in a game decided by only two points. Still, Doncic delivered when the Lakers needed offensive production. top.title: Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Vegas pole despite “ideal” final-lap position
top.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes left Friday night qualifying at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit with the fastest car on track, yet team principal Toto Wolff still had questions to answer. World champion Kimi Antonelli topped Q3 with a 1m33.893s, only to drop to sixth on the grid due to a five-place penalty for taking Mercedes’ updated ADUO turbocharger. Instead of team-mate George Russell inheriting pole, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen snatched top spot with a 1m34.151s - edging Russell’s 1m34.224s by just 0.073 seconds. The result stung after Russell had looked untouchable earlier in the evening, topping final practice with a 1m34.041s that put him 0.911s clear of Antonelli. Complicating matters in Q3, Russell had asked Mercedes for a slipstream from his already-penalised team-mate. Instead, a messy final out-lap left Antonelli trailing the pack, allowing the Italian to pull a tow worth up to 16 km/h down the Strip straight from cars ahead—including Russell. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes Asked after qualifying whether Mercedes should have orchestrated a better tow to aid Russell’s fight for second in the Drivers’ Championship, Wolff dismissed track positioning as the culprit. "Actually, George for me had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front," Wolff said. "We need to find out because I think there was some kind of Turn 7, 8, 9 - whether there was a mistake or something else happened, I don’t know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap because he was quickest all the time." Setting up front-row “cinema” with Verstappen Even without pole, Russell lines up second alongside Verstappen on Saturday night with major championship stakes on the line. Sitting third in the standings and 17 points behind Verstappen, Russell has a prime chance to make serious ground after both Ferraris - Charles Leclerc (11th) and Lewis Hamilton (12th) - were knocked out in Q2. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes Tension between the front-row rivals is already running hot. Late in FP3, Verstappen and Russell tangled wheel-to-wheel at Turn 14 after Verstappen passed the Mercedes and slowed into the corner, prompting the Dutchman to complain over team radio that Russell had "pushed me into the barrier". Following a post-session review, the FIA stewards handed Verstappen a warning for the skirmish. Asked what he expected when the pair launch side by side toward Turn 1, Wolff didn't downplay the prospect of fireworks. "Well, with cinema, if they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching," Wolff said. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

top.description: OKLAHOMA CITY — Racing down the floor, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had his eyes set on the rim. He trucked through Jeremiah Fears to bank in the and-one layup. The two-time MVP walked the baseline and stared at the crowd before he finished the dagger three-point play with 34 seconds left. The Oklahoma City Thunder survived a thriller in a 126-120 win over the New Orleans Pelicans . This was part of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B. In a sport that features plenty of runs, this was one even more roller-coast-esque than usual. The Thunder completely blitzed the Pelicans to get started with a quick 11-0 lead a little over two minutes in. And then New Orleans immediately responded with a 17-4 run. Saddiq Bey buried an outside jumper to cap it off. The Thunder were in a 36-33 deficit after the first quarter. Once again, it was another NBA opponent that completely cooked OKC from the perimeter. This time, it was by one of the worst outside-shooting teams in the league. The second quarter was much the same story. As the Thunder fell behind by double-digit points, they couldn't muster up much offense. Pair that with the Pelicans getting whatever they wanted, it was a recipe for bad vibes. Zion Williamson bully-balled his way to the cup. He looked like his vintage self. Jeremiah Fears' speed helped him dissect OKC's defense. The latter only had 23 points in the second frame. It was in a 64-56 deficit at halftime. Yeesh. The Thunder looked lifeless for most of the first half. For as demoralizing as things have gotten with them, multiply that by 10 for the Pelicans. To finish a putrid first half, Gilgeous-Alexander had a scary-looking fall on a drive to the basket. His shoulder collided with the floor. To start the second half, the Thunder fell into an even deeper hole. Herbert Jones' back-to-back corner 3-pointers were soul-crushers. That put OKC in a 91-76 deficit. The possibility of dropping another gimme stared them straight in the face once again. They salvaged things with a 14-2 run to end the third frame. At that point, the Thunder scored 36 points in the third quarter. The offense finally started to play like an upper-half team. Jared McCain and Bennett Stirtz caught on fire. Aday Mara was a godsend as he played like an old-school seven-footer. They were in a 98-92 deficit with a dozen minutes to go. Another clutch-time scenario was on the verge of materializing. Eventually, McCain erupted the OKC crowd with a game-tying outside jumper. Knotted up at 102 points with nine minutes left, the Thunder played rejuvenated in comparison to their first-half selves. Mara injected some youthful energy as a stop-and-board sequence had him thumping his chest in excitement. When Gilgeous-Alexander checked in, they actually had a three-point lead with eight minutes left — a great spot to be at. top.title: Hopewell football wins instant classic against Propel in WPIAL semifinals
top.description: DORMONT — When the game is on the line and you need a play to win the game, you’re going to call on your best player. That’s exactly the situation that Hopewell found itself in the WPIAL 3A high school football semifinal game against Propel Braddock Hills. After a stop on defense, the team called on junior quarterback and Penn State commit James Armstrong , who took a keeper to the end zone to send the team to the WPIAL championship with a 66-60 double-overtime win on Friday, Nov. 20. “In that situation, nobody is getting the ball other than No. 5 [James Armstrong],” Hopewell interim head coach John Rosa said. “Everyone played great tonight and when you have a Division I quarterback, you put the ball in his hands and let him win you the game.” The semifinal victory for Hopewell will go down as one of the best games in WPIAL playoff history, featuring 126 combined points between the two sides. But it wasn’t a back-and-forth affair throughout, with Hopewell (12-1) having to claw its way back from multiple deficits, including a 16-point hole halfway through the third quarter. After Propel Braddock Hills (8-4) struck for an 11-yard touchdown run by running back Daniel Stephens, Armstrong threw an interception to Mikal Hall, setting up an 85-yard pick-six that — in many games — would have been the nail in the coffin. But not for Hopewell. Following the pick-six, Hopewell answered, with Brody Rock and Avery Bokor combining on a kickoff return, as Rock flipped the ball to Bokor at the Propel 12-yard-line and ran the rest of the way. top.title: No. 8 Pomperaug football rallies past Notre Dame Prep in OT behind Jack Guinipero
top.description: Pomperaug's Caleb McKee (40) goes up to make the game-tying touchdown catch against Notre Dame Prep during a football game at Sacred Heart University on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026. (Dave Stewart/Hearst Connecticut Media) FAIRFIELD - The Pomperaug football team has been stomping all over opponents with a relentless rushing attack this season. But senior Jack Guinipero made one thing clear after the team's latest game. "We can pass, too," he said with a laugh. Guinipero threw a game-tying touchdown pass to Caleb McKee with 51 seconds remaining, then ran for an 8-yard score in overtime to give No. 8-ranked Pomperaug a dramatic 27-20 victory over Notre Dame Prep on Friday at Sacred Heart University's Campus Field. Guinipero even had a hand, literally, on the final play when he knocked away a fourth-down pass from Notre Dame Prep's Jordan Razor. But the tying pass, on a play Guinipero called "28 Rocket Pass," was the biggest highlight, with Guinipero firing a pass from the sidelines into the end zone, and McKee going up under double coverage to make the catch. "That's something we've had on the back burner forever," Guinipero said. "It's one of those plays where, we've got it in our back pocket any time we need it. I hit my favorite receiver, Caleb McKee, an absolute dog and he went over two people for it. Beast, I love to see it." While the pass was the highlight, the running game did the heavy lifting as usual, with Guinipero rushing for 119 yards and a touchdown, Dom Creaco rushing for 80 yards and two touchdowns, and Josh Coughlin rushing for 97 yards. But the Panthers had to overcome three turnovers: two fumbles and an interception by Notre Dame Prep's Razor. "What I loved about this was we overcame that," Pomperaug coach Tom Pereira said. "We kept fighting and fighting, held them out for a two (point attempt) to keep the game within reach, and then we made plays down the stretch. I challenged our defense before this game. Aside from that series coming out of the halftime, we really bottled up their running game and forced them to have to go vertically down the field." The game was the regular-season finale for both teams, which had already unofficially secured playoff berths. Pomperaug (9-1) will be making its first trip to the state tournament since finishing runner-up in the Class L championship in 2009. The Panthers are currently second in Class MM and will likely host a quarterfinal game. top.description: Berlin's Gamaliel Ayizano, 4, blasts through the line during the CIAC football game between Middletown and Berlin high schools.Friday, November 20, 2026, Sage Park, Berlin, Conn. (H John Voorhees III/Hearst Connecticut Media) Two more high school football teams unofficially clinched CIAC playoff spots Friday night, according to GametimeCT calculations, bringing the statewide total to 28 (out of 48) as Week 11 nears its conclusion this weekend. BERLIN (7-3) , last year's Class M champion, clinched a spot in Class SS thanks to its 35-32 victory over rival Middletown at Sage Park. GRANBY/CANTON (8-2) defeated CREC, 41-6 at New Britain, to earn a spot in Class S. They join DANBURY (5-4) , which managed to clinch a spot in Class LL on Thursday afternoon when St. Joseph defeated Westhill, 57-3. Simsbury (8-2) had a chance at clinching a spot in Class L, but concluded its regular season with a 56-28 loss to Glastonbury (3-7). The Trojans (8-2), however, have a favorable path to the playoff based on outside results in the coming days. Middletown (7-3) would have clinched a spot in Class MM had it defeated Berlin, but now must wait for outside results. The CIAC playoff qualifier projections are determined using the CIAC playoff formula , using OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna medium model and verified by GametimeCT using the current CIAC football playoff standings and formula. All qualifiers remain unofficial until the CIAC's football committee meets the day after the regular season concludes on Thanksgiving morning. The playoffs begin Tuesday, Dec. 1 at the sites of the top-four seeds in each of the six divisions. Elsewhere, New Britain (8-2) concluded its regular season with a 24-19 victory over West Haven, a win that clinched one of the top four seeds in Class LL and a home playoff game for the quarterfinals. Pomperaug (9-1) also clinched at least a home quarterfinal in Class MM when it defeated Notre Dame Prep 27-20 in overtime. At least one more playoff spot can be secured Saturday when Bloomfield plays host to Windsor. A win will clinch a Class S spot for the Warhawks. Windsor, last year's Class MM champion, needs a win to keep its faint hopes at defending that title alive. But then came November 20 — the season opener against North. After Reitz led by just one point (43-42) entering the fourth quarter, coach Brock Stone’s group pulled away with a 25-14 effort in the final frame to win 68-56. Rustiness affects Reitz despite win Panthers guard/forward Kierstyn Kaiser led the way with 27 points. The junior showcased an ability to finish inside and a willingness to make plays for others. The Orlando Magic escaped the Brooklyn Nets with a 113-111 NBA Cup victory on Friday night, and for Franz Wagner , the night carried a little extra meaning. Not only did the Magic forward hit the game-winner , but he also faced off against his older brother, Moritz “Moe” Wagner, in an official NBA game for the very first time. The two brothers spent five seasons together in Orlando before Moe signed a two-year, $19 million deal with the Nets in free agency this past summer . That meant Friday’s matchup was the first time the Wagners ever shared the floor as opponents in a game that counted. After the game, Franz admitted that it felt strange to finally see his brother on the other side. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Yes, it was. top.title: JJ Redick Gives Two Reasons For Replacing Jake LaRavia With Ziaire Williams On Lakers’ Starting Lineup
top.description: Nov 9, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick reacts on the sidelines during the game against the Atlanta Hawks at State Farm Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers play the Sacramento Kings tonight at the Crypto.Com Arena. Head coach JJ Redick once again replaced Jake LaRavia with Ziaire Williams in the Lakers’ starting lineup. Ahead of tonight’s game, JJ Redick spoke to the media and explained the decision that initially puzzled many Lakers fans when they made it in their 97-109 loss to the Jazz, which ended their nine-game winning streak. “I felt like, with the group they were going to start, again, we talked to Ziaire and Jake when we were in Milwaukee last week about both of those guys having some flexibility.” “I think Ziaire was in a really good rhythm, and he’s had some good games since he missed some time. We were trying to get him back into a rhythm. He hasn’t really had one over the last three games or so. So, some of it was about that, and some of it was about the matchup.” “Those guys are both easy, low-maintenance winners. They’re not going to be affected by that. I think the message from day one of training camp has always been that every game is going to be a little different. It’s going to present itself differently, and the challenges are going to be different. You have to play the game in front of you, and the guys are bought into that,” Redick explained . Before tonight, Jake LaRavia averaged 5.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 2.2 assists while shooting 47.1% from the field and 46.7% from beyond the arc so far this season. Ziaire Williams averaged 9.5 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 1.8 assists while shooting 56.4% from the field and 44.7% from beyond the arc. It seemed like Jake LaRavia had cemented his role in the Lakers’ starting lineup in 15 games (11 starts). But Ziaire Williams clearly stepped up and made a promising case for a starter role (six starts in 13 games played). The Lakers began the season with three prominently fixed starters whenever they are healthy: Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler. As a result, the wings were always a position to contend for and earn as the season progressed. Given that both power forwards are willing to do whatever it takes to win, this is a good problem for the Lakers: everyone plays so well that they don’t know who to start or who can come off the bench and make an impact. They seem likely to use this position rotationally throughout the season, based on the matchups they expect. It will be interesting to see who the Lakers’ coaching staff decides to start as the playoffs approach later in the season. But down the stretch, it remains to be seen who earns the regular starting power-forward role, as role clarity helps players mold their tendencies accordingly.

top.title: Antonelli fastest but penalty leaves Verstappen on pole
top.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. "I wanted to be on pole but I am probably more pleased with the performance than in Mexico when I was on the front row. "Kimi did a great job and he probably thought it wasn't going to work out so well being so close but with the tow it worked out." Top 10 1. top.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - NOVEMBER 20: James Harden #1 of the Cleveland Cavaliers celebrates after scoring during the third quarter of an Emirates NBA Cup game against the Indiana Pacers at Rocket Arena on November 20, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. The Cavaliers defeated the Pacers 128-119. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images James Harden put on a vintage performance, dropping an electric 51 points, Donovan Mitchell added 20 of his own, and Mario Hezonja put up a double-double off the bench to lead the Cleveland Cavaliers to a 128-119 victory over the visiting Indiana Pacers in an NBA Cup matchup. Cleveland sits just behind the Miami Heat in NBA Cup Group Stage play, while the Pacers fall to 1-2. Harden finished 15-26 from the floor, including 7 for 11 from beyond the arc, to go with six assists and six rebounds. Oh, and in classic fashion, he was also 14-14 from the free throw line. Cleveland now sits just over .500 at 9-8, beating an Indiana team that was still without star guard Tyrese Haliburton. The Cavs did not have forward Evan Mobley, who is undergoing treatment for a great toe sprain. Peyton Watson returned from a one-game absence due to a back injury, and provided 15 points, four rebounds, and three assists. The two teams were neck and neck in the first half, with the Cavs holding a slight one-point advantage at the break. But it was the 37-year-old Harden who took over in the third quarter, helping Cleveland outscore Indiana 43-23 in the frame. Harden’s 51-point effort, the 26th of his career, puts him past Kobe Bryant for third on the NBA’s all-time 50-point game list. “My idol, the person I watched growing up,” Harden said in a postgame interview when told he passed Bryant on the all-time list. Harden has been playing much better of late following his slow start, something that the former MVP has built into his conditioning strategy of playing into game shape. Mitchell’s 20 points mostly came in the second half, but he helped apply pressure in that “Cavalanche” of a third quarter that allowed Cleveland to pull away. While most of the attention will go toward the 50-point effort, Hezonja’s ten points and ten rebounds off the bench continue a stretch of solid play. When the Cavs play well, and with energy, chances are that Hezonja is part of the reason why. He has made smart passes, rebounded the basketball well, and seems very comfortable on offense getting to his spots around the paint. It won’t be the headline of this game, but Cleveland must be pleased with their signing of Hezonja this past offseason. The Cavs also moved to 2-1 in NBA Cup play and put themselves in position to advance out of the Group Stage, just behind the Heat. top.title: Clemson commit drills 58-yard field goal, walk-off winner in Florida playoff stunner
top.description: Brandin Gallaway has the leg to change a football game. Friday night, the Clemson commit did it twice . The Palmetto senior kicker drilled a 58-yard field goal to tie the game before halftime, then came through with a 34-yard kick as time expired to give the Tigers a dramatic 12-10 upset of Tampa Bay Tech in the Class 5A-Region 3 semifinals . Gallaway accounted for all 12 of Palmetto's points, converting all four of his field-goal attempts to send the Tigers (11-1) into the regional final. His biggest kick of the first half came with 35 seconds remaining. Facing a long attempt, Gallaway connected from 58 yards to tie the game at 6-6 and give Palmetto momentum heading into the break. Tampa Bay Tech had taken the lead late in the first quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Martavius Conway Jr., but missed the extra point. Gallaway put Palmetto ahead with a 42-yard field goal with 3:41 remaining in the third quarter. Tampa Bay Tech answered with a 29-yard field goal with four minutes left in the game, setting up a dramatic finish. The Tigers' ensuing possession stalled near midfield, but their defense gave Gallaway another opportunity. Palmetto's defense flushed Conway out of the pocket, and Jordan Allen stepped in front of his pass at the Tampa Bay Tech 42-yard line, returning the interception to the 34. Palmetto moved the ball to the 17-yard line before sending Gallaway onto the field with three seconds remaining. The senior, like he had all night, delivered once more for safe measure. His 34-yard attempt sailed through the uprights as time expired, sending Palmetto into the regional final and capping a four-field-goal performance that will be difficult to forget. Palmetto will travel to face top-seeded Armwood next Friday. Armwood advanced with a 37-12 victory over Sumner. nigeria.description: By Dickson Omobola Federal Government’s proposed mandatory biometric checks for domestic air passengers from January 1, 2027, have come under scrutiny less than five days after the plan was announced, with passengers and industry observers warning that the policy could make air travel more difficult. They insisted that the plan appeared rushed and had not been properly thought through, particularly as the festive travel season would still be ongoing when the policy takes effect. They also feared that its implementation could trigger a repeat of the chaos that followed the introduction of the Go Cashless payment system, which caused hours of gridlock at airports in Lagos and Abuja. In March, the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, introduced an electronic payment system known as Go Cashless at the toll gate of two of the country’s busiest airports. Its rollout left passengers travelling through the airports in Lagos and Abuja stranded for hours, triggering massive gridlock, missed flights and widespread frustration. Keyamo warned that airlines that fail to comply with the directive would not be allowed to board passengers from January 1, 2027. Known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, v-PASS, the biometric identity verification system is linked to the National Identification Number, NIN, of Nigerians. It is designed exclusively for domestic flights, with all passengers required to provide their NIN during check-in. Passengers are also expected to pay additional charges for the service. nigeria.title: 6.7 magnitude earthquake hits Peru
nigeria.description: A 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Peru on Friday, Peru’s Defense Ministry said, with preliminary reports indicating minor damage and no fatalities. The earthquake occurred at 7:09 pm (0009 GMT Saturday), 30 kilometers (18 miles) northwest of the city of Junin, at a depth of 129 kilometers. The United States Geological Survey (USGS) also measured the quake to have a magnitude of 6.7, but estimated its depth to be only 108 kilometers. Peru’s Defense Minister, Rafael Belaunde, reported that after the earthquake “minor damage was reported to homes in different parts of Junin, as well as interruptions of electricity service and restrictions on highway transit.” Belaunde added that there had been “no harm to people or impacts to their bodies and health.” AFP journalists in Lima saw hundreds of people evacuating buildings in the Miraflores district during the quake. The earthquake was also felt in the capital Lima, as well as Ancash, Ica, Ucayali, Cerro de Pasco, Huanuco and Callao. Peru’s National Emergency Operation Center (COEN) reported the quake was felt with moderate to strong intensity and that “monitoring continues in vulnerable areas.” Hernando Tavera, the president of the Peruvian Geophysical Institute, told AFP: “The ground shaking was intense. We have no reports of damage at the moment, but there have been landslides and rockfalls on the hillsides.” Peru is situated on the so-called Pacific Ring of Fire — an arc of intense seismic activity stretching from Japan through Southeast Asia and across the Pacific basin. Seismologists say Peru experiences at least 400 earthquakes per year, three-quarters of which are so weak people do not feel them. A 5.1-magnitude earthquake in the Junin region in July killed six people, injured 32 others and destroyed 52 homes. nigeria.title: Why obesity hits men harder than women – Study
nigeria.description: By Shola Ogundipe Scientists have uncovered a hidden biological difference in the fat tissue of males and females that could help explain why obesity triggers different health consequences in men and women. The discovery suggests that the battle against obesity may be playing out differently beneath the skin, with immune cells living inside body fat either helping to protect against inflammation and metabolic disorders or making them worse, depending on biological sex. Researchers at the University of California, Riverside, US, found that a group of immune cells known as eosinophils, traditionally associated with allergies and asthma, perform different functions in the fat tissue of male and female mice. While certain populations of these cells appear to protect against obesity-related inflammation, others may contribute to harmful metabolic changes. The study, titled “Single-cell heterogeneity of adipose eosinophils is shaped by sex and RELMα and linked to macrophage communication networks in obesity”, was funded by the National Institutes of Health, the UCR School of Medicine and the California Institute for Regenerative Medicine. The findings, published in the journal PNAS Nexus, challenge the longstanding assumption that eosinophils are largely similar in structure and function. They also raise questions about whether obesity treatments targeting the immune system should be designed differently for men and women. Led by biomedical scientists Meera Nair and Adam Godzik, the study used high-resolution single-cell sequencing to examine how individual immune cells behave in fat tissue. What emerged was an unexpected picture. The researchers identified six distinct populations of eosinophils in adipose tissue, each with its own genetic activity and potentially different biological functions. The discovery suggests that these cells are not simply passive occupants of body fat. Some may help maintain metabolic health, while others may contribute to the inflammatory processes associated with obesity. “Eosinophils are more complex than we once thought,” said Nair, a professor of biomedical sciences at UCR’s School of Medicine. She explained that identifying and activating the biological pathways responsible for producing protective eosinophils could open new possibilities for improving metabolic health. But perhaps the most striking finding was the difference between male and female mice. Female mice had a population of eosinophils that appeared to work more effectively with macrophages, another group of immune cells found in fat tissue. Their cooperation seemed to support a healthier environment within fat tissue and better metabolic function. Male mice, however, showed a different response when exposed to a high-fat diet. They were more likely to develop eosinophil populations associated with inflammation, alongside weaker protective activity in their fat tissue. nigeria.description: * Bloodline, Ballot Box, and the Bedroom: Lessons from Kano’s High Stakes Political Divorce A marriage rarely belongs to two people alone. In northern Nigeria, where zumunci binds families through kinship, mutual obligations and family honour, marriage often carries expectations that extend far beyond the couple. For twenty years, the union between Kano State Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf and Zainab Musa Kwankwaso appeared to demonstrate that bloodline and political loyalty could coexist under one roof. Today, that roof has given way. The breakdown of the marriage between Governor Yusuf and Zainab, niece of his estranged political mentor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, and raised in the former governor’s household, is more than a headline from Government House. It raises an uncomfortable question: what happens when the political alliance connecting two families collapses, but the marriage binding them is left caught in its aftermath? To understand the significance of this separation, one must understand how political trust is built in Kano. Political relationships are not always sustained by ambition and party loyalty alone. Sometimes, they are reinforced through family connections. When Zainab and Abba Yusuf married on July 29, 2006, Yusuf was already deeply embedded in Kwankwaso’s political circle, having served as his personal and special assistant during Kwankwaso’s first tenure as governor and subsequently during his tenure as Minister of Defence. Zainab, raised in Kwankwaso’s household, was not simply marrying an ambitious politician. Their union connected two families whose fortunes were closely intertwined. Over twenty years and six children, the marriage became one of the most personal bonds surrounding the Kwankwasiyya movement. Yusuf’s years of loyalty and proximity to Kwankwaso eventually culminated in his emergence as the latter’s preferred successor and his election as governor in 2023. The trusted lieutenant had become governor, with the backing of the political establishment that had shaped his career. nigeria.description: By Chioma Gabriel, Editor, Special Features It is often said that women are a necessary evil, a desirable calamity and a domestic peril. It all depends on where one is standing. In traditional African societies, a woman’s place was said to be in the kitchen, from where she was expected to work her way into her husband’s heart through his stomach. Women were traditionally expected to be seen but not heard. They were like shadows trailing their husbands, with little or no opportunity to express opinions on matters affecting the family and society. They were often regarded as acquired possessions whose primary responsibilities were to bear children and provide labour on the farms. They had little or no say in the scheme of things. A similar pattern appears in some biblical accounts, where headcounts excluded women and children. When Jesus fed the 5,000 and the 4,000, the recorded figures referred to the men, with women and children excluded from the count. In the early Christian community, Paul’s instruction required women to remain silent in church and ask their husbands questions at home. Although interpretations of this passage differ among Christian scholars, it has historically been cited to support restrictions on women’s public religious participation. Despite these historical and cultural limitations, women have, in different ways, exercised considerable influence over men, including their husbands. Eve persuaded Adam to eat the forbidden fruit after the serpent tempted her in the Garden of Eden. Jezebel manipulated her husband, King Ahab, and orchestrated the murder of Naboth to acquire his vineyard. Delilah used persistent pressure and deception to make Samson reveal the secret of his extraordinary strength. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. entertainment.title: Visa Report Identifies Opportunity to Integrate Digital Payments with SMEs Business Operations in Nigeria
entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. Nigerian music history just added another major chapter in Los Angeles, and the celebration has been loud from Lagos to London. For Fela Kuti, nearly three decades after his passing in 1997, this induction makes him the first African-born solo artist to enter the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Honoured posthumously in the Early Influence category—five years after he was first nominated in 2021—the recognition celebrates how he fused West African rhythms with jazz, funk, and soul to create Afrobeat, using his voice and horns to confront social and political injustice across classics like “Zombie”, “Water No Get Enemy”, and “Sorrow, Tears and Blood”. sports.title: Toto Wolff wants answers after George Russell misses Vegas pole despite “ideal” final-lap position
sports.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes left Friday night qualifying at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit with the fastest car on track, yet team principal Toto Wolff still had questions to answer. World champion Kimi Antonelli topped Q3 with a 1m33.893s, only to drop to sixth on the grid due to a five-place penalty for taking Mercedes’ updated ADUO turbocharger. Instead of team-mate George Russell inheriting pole, Red Bull’s Max Verstappen snatched top spot with a 1m34.151s - edging Russell’s 1m34.224s by just 0.073 seconds. The result stung after Russell had looked untouchable earlier in the evening, topping final practice with a 1m34.041s that put him 0.911s clear of Antonelli. Complicating matters in Q3, Russell had asked Mercedes for a slipstream from his already-penalised team-mate. Instead, a messy final out-lap left Antonelli trailing the pack, allowing the Italian to pull a tow worth up to 16 km/h down the Strip straight from cars ahead—including Russell. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes Asked after qualifying whether Mercedes should have orchestrated a better tow to aid Russell’s fight for second in the Drivers’ Championship, Wolff dismissed track positioning as the culprit. "Actually, George for me had the perfect position. He was four seconds behind the car in front," Wolff said. "We need to find out because I think there was some kind of Turn 7, 8, 9 - whether there was a mistake or something else happened, I don’t know, to be honest, but it looked like the ideal position for a pole lap because he was quickest all the time." Setting up front-row “cinema” with Verstappen Even without pole, Russell lines up second alongside Verstappen on Saturday night with major championship stakes on the line. Sitting third in the standings and 17 points behind Verstappen, Russell has a prime chance to make serious ground after both Ferraris - Charles Leclerc (11th) and Lewis Hamilton (12th) - were knocked out in Q2. Late in FP3, Verstappen and Russell tangled wheel-to-wheel at Turn 14 after Verstappen passed the Mercedes and slowed into the corner, prompting the Dutchman to complain over team radio that Russell had "pushed me into the barrier". Following a post-session review, the FIA stewards handed Verstappen a warning for the skirmish. Asked what he expected when the pair launch side by side toward Turn 1, Wolff didn't downplay the prospect of fireworks. "Well, with cinema, if they try to go through the first corners together, we shall be watching," Wolff said. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

But senior Jack Guinipero made one thing clear after the team's latest game. "We can pass, too," he said with a laugh. Guinipero threw a game-tying touchdown pass to Caleb McKee with 51 seconds remaining, then ran for an 8-yard score in overtime to give No. 8-ranked Pomperaug a dramatic 27-20 victory over Notre Dame Prep on Friday at Sacred Heart University's Campus Field. Guinipero even had a hand, literally, on the final play when he knocked away a fourth-down pass from Notre Dame Prep's Jordan Razor. sports.title: JJ Redick Gives Two Reasons For Replacing Jake LaRavia With Ziaire Williams On Lakers’ Starting Lineup
sports.description: Nov 9, 2026; Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick reacts on the sidelines during the game against the Atlanta Hawks at State Farm Arena. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers play the Sacramento Kings tonight at the Crypto.Com Arena. Head coach JJ Redick once again replaced Jake LaRavia with Ziaire Williams in the Lakers’ starting lineup. Ahead of tonight’s game, JJ Redick spoke to the media and explained the decision that initially puzzled many Lakers fans when they made it in their 97-109 loss to the Jazz, which ended their nine-game winning streak. “I felt like, with the group they were going to start, again, we talked to Ziaire and Jake when we were in Milwaukee last week about both of those guys having some flexibility.” “I think Ziaire was in a really good rhythm, and he’s had some good games since he missed some time. We were trying to get him back into a rhythm. He hasn’t really had one over the last three games or so. So, some of it was about that, and some of it was about the matchup.” “Those guys are both easy, low-maintenance winners. They’re not going to be affected by that. I think the message from day one of training camp has always been that every game is going to be a little different. It’s going to present itself differently, and the challenges are going to be different. You have to play the game in front of you, and the guys are bought into that,” Redick explained . Before tonight, Jake LaRavia averaged 5.8 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 2.2 assists while shooting 47.1% from the field and 46.7% from beyond the arc so far this season. Ziaire Williams averaged 9.5 points, 2.4 rebounds, and 1.8 assists while shooting 56.4% from the field and 44.7% from beyond the arc. It seemed like Jake LaRavia had cemented his role in the Lakers’ starting lineup in 15 games (11 starts). But Ziaire Williams clearly stepped up and made a promising case for a starter role (six starts in 13 games played). The Lakers began the season with three prominently fixed starters whenever they are healthy: Luka Doncic, Austin Reaves, and Walker Kessler. As a result, the wings were always a position to contend for and earn as the season progressed. Given that both power forwards are willing to do whatever it takes to win, this is a good problem for the Lakers: everyone plays so well that they don’t know who to start or who can come off the bench and make an impact. They seem likely to use this position rotationally throughout the season, based on the matchups they expect. It will be interesting to see who the Lakers’ coaching staff decides to start as the playoffs approach later in the season. But down the stretch, it remains to be seen who earns the regular starting power-forward role, as role clarity helps players mold their tendencies accordingly.

sports.title: Antonelli fastest but penalty leaves Verstappen on pole
sports.description: Kimi Antonelli won both the previous two grands prix in the United States this season, in Miami and Austin [Getty Images] Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix but a grid penalty will hand pole position to Red Bull's Max Verstappen. Antonelli, running at the back of the pack of cars in qualifying and maximising his tow, beat Verstappen by 0.258 seconds. But the new world champion has a five-place grid penalty for using more than permitted number of engine components and will start sixth. The Italian's team-mate George Russell was just 0.073secs behind Verstappen and will start alongside the Dutchman on the front row. McLaren's Lando Norris qualified fourth, and will start third, ahead of Red Bull's Isack Hadjar. Both Ferraris were eliminated in the second session and qualified 11th and 12th with Charles Leclerc ahead of Lewis Hamilton. Each will be promoted a place by a 10-place penalty for McLaren's Oscar Piastri, who qualified seventh. Racing Bulls' rookie Arvid Lindblad, sixth fastest, is the last driver to be promoted as a result of Antonelli's penalty. Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson will start seventh with Alpine's Pierre Gasly eighth and Franco Colapinto ninth. Drivers limited to 27 laps for tyres in Qatar Antonelli's final run did not start auspiciously as he and Russell became tangled up with the Alpines and Racing Bulls as they sought the best track position to optimise the slipstream effect. Antonelli ended up the last driver to run and made it to the line with only one second to spare before the chequered flag, one second behind Lindblad. Normally, being so close to the car in front would be a compromise but in Las Vegas it magnified the tow effect and Antonelli leapt to the front. "That was all the tow," he said over the radio after being told he was on pole. "Starting the lap, I was only one second behind the car in front and I thought I was screwed," he said. "But the tow is so powerful here." Verstappen, who has won two of the three Las Vegas Grands Prix, said: "I have been struggling with some weird issues that were also in the car in Brazil and just trying to get my head around how to deal with that. "In qualifying we managed to make it work. Had a solid qualifying. My first lap in qualifying was pretty much as good as it could be with the tow, so to be on the front row is good for us. "It was solid in the corners, and you have a bit of dirty air, but it is insane how much you gain on the straights." Russell had looked in the running for the pole, but was happy with his session despite missing out. "Overall it's been a very solid session and a solid day," he said. "I wanted to be on pole but I am probably more pleased with the performance than in Mexico when I was on the front row. "Kimi did a great job and he probably thought it wasn't going to work out so well being so close but with the tow it worked out." Top 10 1. Cleveland sits just behind the Miami Heat in NBA Cup Group Stage play, while the Pacers fall to 1-2. sports.title: Clemson commit drills 58-yard field goal, walk-off winner in Florida playoff stunner
sports.description: Brandin Gallaway has the leg to change a football game. Friday night, the Clemson commit did it twice . The Palmetto senior kicker drilled a 58-yard field goal to tie the game before halftime, then came through with a 34-yard kick as time expired to give the Tigers a dramatic 12-10 upset of Tampa Bay Tech in the Class 5A-Region 3 semifinals . Gallaway accounted for all 12 of Palmetto's points, converting all four of his field-goal attempts to send the Tigers (11-1) into the regional final. His biggest kick of the first half came with 35 seconds remaining. Facing a long attempt, Gallaway connected from 58 yards to tie the game at 6-6 and give Palmetto momentum heading into the break. Tampa Bay Tech had taken the lead late in the first quarter on a 15-yard touchdown pass from Martavius Conway Jr., but missed the extra point. Gallaway put Palmetto ahead with a 42-yard field goal with 3:41 remaining in the third quarter. Tampa Bay Tech answered with a 29-yard field goal with four minutes left in the game, setting up a dramatic finish. The Tigers' ensuing possession stalled near midfield, but their defense gave Gallaway another opportunity. Palmetto's defense flushed Conway out of the pocket, and Jordan Allen stepped in front of his pass at the Tampa Bay Tech 42-yard line, returning the interception to the 34. Palmetto moved the ball to the 17-yard line before sending Gallaway onto the field with three seconds remaining. The senior, like he had all night, delivered once more for safe measure. His 34-yard attempt sailed through the uprights as time expired, sending Palmetto into the regional final and capping a four-field-goal performance that will be difficult to forget. Palmetto will travel to face top-seeded Armwood next Friday. Armwood advanced with a 37-12 victory over Sumner. technology.title: Amazon's split personality: AWS embraces bot commerce while main site enforces bans
technology.description: Amazon is of two minds when it comes to automated purchasing. The ecommerce giant has been busy banning AI shopping agents from accessing its website. Meanwhile, AWS Marketplace has opened its door to bot-based buying. "Buying software and data through AWS Marketplace just got easier, for you and for the AI agents working alongside you," said Mya Papolu, product marketing manager for AWS Marketplace and Partner Services at Amazon Web Services, in a blog post this week. "For re:Invent 2026, we’re launching capabilities designed to reduce friction across the buying journey." For a company that has blocked bots from Google, Meta, and OpenAI, and sued Perplexity to keep its AI-encumbered Comet browser away, the openness of AWS Marketplace to agentic commerce invites questions. We asked Amazon to explain but we've not heard back. AWS Marketplace is allowing AI agents to scour its site and buy some cloud software products using the x402 agentic payment protocol , which is supported by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments. Introduced by Coinbase and Cloudflare , x402 got handed over to the Linux Foundation earlier this year, and now has support from a variety of tech platforms, including AWS, Google, Stripe, and various blockchain networks. About a week ago, Brave Software announced support for x402 payments through its search API. AWS requires sellers to register with AWS Marketplace and to integrate the AWS Marketplace x402 SDK to enable agentic product purchases. Transactions settle in USD through AWS billing so existing spending controls can be applied. And now, customers in the US can buy some AWS Marketplace software without an AWS account; instead they're asked to provide an email or social media login, and a credit card. While AWS Marketplace today lists mainly familiar software categories (Business Applications, Data & Analytics, DevOps, Infrastructure Software, and so on), AWS has a broader product inventory in mind. Beyond software and APIs, the biz sees a future in selling content and data. Papolu announced that AWS is now selling " data as a service ." "Data providers can list their offerings in AWS Marketplace, making commercial data accessible to both human teams and the agents working alongside them via the AWS Marketplace website, APIs, and MCP server," she said. technology.title: PHP 8.6: Things are gonna get a lot more strict around here
technology.description: On Thursday, PHP version 8.6 was released on its usual yearly schedule, popping up as if the web scripting language hadn’t been under intense scrutiny this past month. For those who missed it: a swarm of unearthed vulnerabilities has plagued PHP since October, allowing unauthenticated attackers to crash PHP workers or execute arbitrary code on the server. Users of every PHP-based application, including WordPress, Laravel, and Symfony, had to scramble to update their PHP instances. The PHP core development community, along with the PHP Foundation , responded with a coordinated release of patched versions of PHP ( 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and the new 8.6) that closed seven critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws in one sweep. In addition to patching specific exploitable holes in the PHP engine, the new version of PHP also tamps down some of PHP’s historically liberal configuration settings. Lucky for PHP, and for the rest of us, core developer Jörg Sowa called out these lax settings in June, when he posted a proposal to set more security-friendly defaults. Sowa saw that three configuration settings of PHP’s session extension – Strict Mode, HttpOnly, and SameSite – were designed to boost security but shipped “with defaults that leave applications unnecessarily exposed.” No cookies for impostors In a retrospective posted last month, the PHP Foundation admitted that consensus-driven gridlock had stalled complex fixes for months and vowed to get patches out the door sooner, should the vulnerabilities leak ahead of the agreed-upon deadline . Code-wise, Sowa’s proposal to harden PHP settings was accepted for PHP 8.6. These changes won’t stop the flood of AI-generated CVEs, but at least these holes will be more difficult to exploit. For Strict Mode, PHP will no longer accept uninitialized session IDs that it didn’t create itself. Before, an attacker could just plant a made-up session ID on the victim to gain entry. “The built-in files handler checks whether a session file for that ID exists on disk; because an attacker-planted ID has no corresponding file, a fresh random ID is generated instead,” Sowa wrote. Furthermore, PHP will now, by default, add the HttpOnly flag to its session Set-Cookie header, blocking client-side JavaScript from reading the session ID, which could otherwise be stolen to masquerade as the user. Believe it or not, any script on the page could read it before. Finally, the server will withhold session cookies on cross-site POST requests, as well as for subrequests and iframes. “Without it, a forged form or link on an attacker-controlled site can trigger authenticated requests using the victim’s session,” Sowa wrote. Going forward, cookies will only be sent on same-site requests and top-level GET navigations, such as clicking a normal link. technology.title: Visa, Mastercard theft included info useful for phishing, but not draining bank accounts, say researchers
technology.description: Visa and Mastercard customer info leaked by the data thieves and extortionists who claim to have stolen it from the financial giants doesn’t include card numbers, passwords, or home addresses. On Thursday, Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase confirmed to The Register that they are investigating third-party breaches that may involve customer information. Ransomware and extortion crew n0n claimed to be responsible for all three, and on Thursday published samples of the stolen files – data-theft groups typically leak some of the compromised data ahead of the official extortion deadline in an effort to put more pressure on victim companies to pay the ransom demand. Researchers at SOCRadar, a threat-intelligence firm that has been tracking n0n since it emerged in September, have parsed all 14 files in the n0n’s published Visa and Mastercard archives, and told us that the files don’t contain any financial details belonging to banking customers. “We found no card numbers, expiry dates, CVVs, passwords, dates of birth, or home addresses in any file,” Ensar Seker, SOCRadar chief information security officer, told The Register . “Visa's statement that no card numbers were affected matches our scan.” Mastercard previously said that stolen data included a “limited amount of email addresses – non-payments information” from a subset of cardholders in a benefits program. According to SOCRadar’s analysis, the leaked files do contain mobile numbers, Bank Identification Number (BIN) prefixes, and dated airline, hotel, and restaurant bookings. So while the data doesn’t include card or account numbers that crooks could use to drain customers' bank accounts or rack up massive credit card bills, “that detail is what a fraudster needs to pose as a concierge desk or a bank,” in an email or voice-phishing social engineering attack, Seker said. It’s also worth noting that the published files only represent about 0.4 percent of the data n0n claims to have hoovered up in the breach: about 4.3 GB and 1.9 million marketing events. “So a further release is possible,” according to Seker. Plus, both datasets come from the same upstream provider, we’re told. They use the same 27-column booking layout, placeholder text, and CRM ID format, Seker said, noting that the most recent record in each stops 69 seconds apart on Oct 26. “This looks like two card programs run on one provider's platform,” he said. “The pattern looks like a batch copy from a marketing and reporting store.” Customer data has left the building The security shop hasn’t analyzed the Chase customer data that n0n also claimed to have published. None of the secrets had ever been used before, and he controlled the infrastructure that received any requests using the credentials. He then seeded each secret into exactly one prompt sent to a single provider. In the event any of the secrets were leaked, these “canaries”—so called because they resemble the role of that bird when taken into coal mines—would allow Moore to identify each link in the chain that was responsible. "Google and Apple are integrating agentic capabilities like Gemini Intelligence with Google Gemini and Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI deep into their operating systems," wrote Whittaker in a blog post . "In order to gain access to information about you, these OS AI agents 'scan' the information that’s on your screen. In doing so, your Signal data is captured, then made available to these agentic systems in order to allow them to answer your questions and do your bidding." Updates to Signal's iOS and Android apps now include controls that by default block Siri on iOS and Gemini and other agents on Android from taking screenshots, which AI agents process using optical character recognition to extract text. Screenshot blocking, Whittaker concedes, is only a partial solution since AI agents may have other ways to access application data through the device file system. "We want to be very clear: it is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy," she said. "Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience. This is also the reason we are currently unable to implement these protections on macOS." technology.title: Watching as a giant star swallowed its neighbor and exploded
technology.description: In the Andromeda Galaxy, a giant star about seven times as massive as the Sun spent nearly a decade slowly swallowing its much smaller companion. The process, known as common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some of the tightest pairs of stars in the Universe form, but no one had ever caught it in the act. In a new Nature study, astronomers led by Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University, finally witnessed the entire spectacle from the decades before it began to the eruption that ended it in late 2025. “It lasts for a few years, maybe a few decades,” Karambelkar said. “Stars evolve on time scales of millions of years. So, it's really like a blip on the entire cosmic time scale.” Shared envelopes Some pairs of stars orbit so close to each other that they could not have formed at that distance, so their orbits must have shrunk. Common envelope evolution is the leading explanation for that shrinkage. When one star in a binary grows old, it expands into a giant, and its outer layers can engulf its companion. The two then share a single, loosely bound envelope of gas. As the engulfed star drags through it, it loses orbital energy to friction and spirals inward. Depending on how much of the envelope gets lost, the pair either ends up in a much tighter orbit or merges. Read full article Comments

Mathematician Bernhard Riemann suspected this was the case, but he never proved it conclusively, and his mathematical successors have spent more than a century trying to demonstrate that he was right. The Riemann hypothesis may now be proven , and it could reveal the most basic structure of our number system, while also opening the door for a new understanding of the vast world of mathematical functions. Read more Mathematicians and AI in behind-the-scenes battle over what’s true In 1859, Riemann made a casual remark about a mathematical function in his memoir, qualifying a statement about it as “very probably” true. The fact that he never proved it more definitively has held the world of mathematics in suspense ever since, and the “Riemann hypothesis” became the field’s most famous and stubbornly unsolved problem – until now. A new AI-assisted proof by Levent Alpöge at Anthropic may have just ended a whole era of mathematics by confirming Riemann’s hunch from nearly 200 years ago. “This result, if true, will be the culmination of a struggle thousands of mathematicians have attempted in the past,” says Christopher Hughes at the University of York in the UK. The proof of the Reimann hypothesis is also one of the Clay Mathematics Institute ’s Millennium Prize Problems, each of which comes with a $1 million prize for a solution. Advertisement The Riemann hypothesis has loomed so large over mathematicians for decades because it concerns mathematics’ most simple yet hard-to-understand objects: prime numbers . These are numbers that aren’t divisible by any number other than 1 and themselves, and any number can be built by multiplying primes. In this way, primes are the bones of all systems of numbers; everything is built on top of them. But how primes are distributed among all numbers is, on the face of it, unpredictable. This is where Riemann made an intervention. He hypothesised that the way primes are spaced throughout the number line can be inferred from another set of numbers, now tied to a mathematical function called the Riemann zeta function. science.description:
Tereza is a London-based science and technology journalist, aspiring fiction writer and amateur gymnast. Originally from Prague, the Czech Republic, she spent the first seven years of her career working as a reporter, script-writer and presenter for various TV programmes of the Czech Public Service Television. She later took a career break to pursue further education and added a Master's in Science from the International Space University, France, to her Bachelor's in Journalism and Master's in Cultural Anthropology from Prague's Charles University. She worked as a reporter at the Engineering and Technology magazine, freelanced for a range of publications including Live Science, Space.com, Professional Engineering, Via Satellite and Space News and served as a maternity cover science editor at the European Space Agency.

Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment. Two such researchers are Florian Rabitz, a professor of climate and technology governance at Vilnius University in Lithuania, and Xiao-Shan Yap, an assistant professor of Earth-space sustainability at Utrecht University in the Netherlands. In a piece published last month in the journal Global Environmental Politics , the pair call for "robust international regulations" and "broad and inclusive deliberation" to allow the global community to carefully consider the impact of economic activities on the moon. In addition to the threat to the scientifically priceless lunar landscape, the researchers also object to the colonization of the moon by a small number of powerful players — namely China, the U.S. and their respective close allies. "With the moon it's absolutely clear that whoever is doing the big infrastructure work is going to be asserting their position, including by defining their own exclusive territories," Rabitz said in a statement . "That shouldn't be the Wild West." Rabitz pointed out that, although the United Nations' 1967 Outer Space Treaty prevents individual nations from appropriating the moon, Earth's natural satellite and its valuable resources are unlikely to remain truly neutral territory if its exploitation is going to be led by a small number of powerful nations.
